title: Behold the Throne of Grace
description: Behold the Throne of Grace in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 33, “Ask what I shall give thee. 1Ki 3:5”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the throne of grace! The pro-mise calls me near; There Je-sus shows a smil-ing face, And waits to an-swer prayer.

lines: There Jesus shows a smiling face,
Provides for those who come to God,
My soul ask what thou wilt,
Thou canst not be too bold;
Since his own blood for thee he spilt,
His love and pow'r can bless;
To praying souls he always grants,
Lord open thou thy bounteous hand,
I ask to serve thee here below,
Teach me to live by faith,
Let me victorious be in death,
Cheerful the world's poor toys I leave,
To them who know not thee.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
